title: Kerusi State Delta
description: Incremental seat status updates for a push transport such as WebSocket or SSE (Kerusi v1.0, RFC section 5.2).

kerusi.description: Spec version this document conforms to (section 7).

sessionId.description: Matches KerusiSession.id. Same either/or rule as KerusiState.

updatedAt.description: RFC 3339 date-time (section 5.1.1), strictly increasing per session/map, so a consumer can detect and discard an out-of-order delta.
updatedAt.$comment: Monotonicity is a property of a stream of deltas, not of a single document, and cannot be checked by this schema. A consumer that detects a gap or an out-of-order delta SHOULD discard its accumulated state and re-fetch a full KerusiState (section 5.2). Section 5.1.1 requires an RFC 3339 date-time, which is exactly what 'format: date-time' checks - so this is a direct transcription, not a narrowing. Forms that section 5.1.1 rules out, such as '2026-08-17T09:14Z' with seconds omitted or the basic format '20260817T091400Z', are correctly rejected. Note that per RFC 3339 section 5.6 some validators still accept a space in place of 'T'.

changes.description: Keyed by Seat.id. Every entry IS an explicit change; there is no default. An explicit { "status": "available" } entry signals a seat reverting, and a seat's absence means 'unchanged' - the opposite of KerusiState's sparse rule (section 5.2).
changes.$comment: An empty changes object is valid: section 5.2 RECOMMENDS heartbeat deltas with a no-op changes object and an advancing updatedAt to keep sequencing gaps rare. Every key MUST match a Seat.id in the referenced KerusiMap; that is a cross-document check for a custom validator.

allOf.title: Session-or-map scope (section 5.2)
allOf.description: Exactly one of sessionId or mapId MUST be present.

SeatStatus.title: SeatStatus
SeatStatus.description: The status of one seat (section 5.1). Identical in shape to KerusiState's SeatStatus.

holdExpires.description: RFC 3339 date-time (section 5.1.1). Meaningful only when status is 'held'.
holdExpires.$comment: Section 5.1.1 requires an RFC 3339 date-time, which is exactly what 'format: date-time' checks - so this is a direct transcription, not a narrowing. Forms that section 5.1.1 rules out, such as '2026-08-17T09:14Z' with seconds omitted or the basic format '20260817T091400Z', are correctly rejected. Note that per RFC 3339 section 5.6 some validators still accept a space in place of 'T'.
